slides.title: Wrong size should not mean *a lost sale.*
slides.sub: How a size-exchange flow offers a swap before a refund.

slides.title: Ask why, in the return form
slides.body: Add one required field: *too small, too big, changed my mind, faulty.* The answer decides what happens next.

slides.title: Too small or too big? Check stock
slides.body: The workflow looks up the same style one size up or down in Shopify before offering anything.

slides.title: Offer the swap first
slides.body: If the size is in stock, send a WhatsApp or email: *keep the sale, ship the new size when the old pair is on its way back.*

slides.title: Hold the stock for 48 hours
slides.body: Reserve the pair so it is still there when they say yes. Release it automatically if they do not.

slides.title: Refund only when they choose it
slides.body: No stock, or the customer prefers money back? The normal refund path runs. *Nothing is forced.*

slides.title: Your automation failed at 2am. *Who found out?*
slides.sub: If the answer is a customer, read on.

slides.title: Silent failures are the default
slides.body: An expired login, a changed field, an API limit. Most tools *log* the error and move on. Nobody is told.

slides.title: Add an error path to every workflow
slides.body: n8n has an *Error Trigger* workflow. Make.com has error handlers per module. Zapier emails you about failed Zaps. Use them.

slides.title: Send the alert to a person, not an inbox
slides.body: Slack, WhatsApp or SMS to the person who owns the process, with the order or record ID in the message.

slides.title: Check daily that it ran
slides.body: A failure alert cannot fire if the workflow never started. Add a simple *did it run today?* check.

slides.title: Not sure your workflows would tell you?
slides.sub: Send us a list of your automations. We'll point out the silent ones.

captions.ig:
The most common automation problem we see is not a broken workflow. It's a broken workflow nobody knew about.

Four fixes:
01 Accept that failures are silent by default
02 Add an error path to every workflow (n8n Error Trigger, Make.com error handlers, Zapier failure emails)
03 Alert a named person with the record ID
04 Check daily that the workflow actually ran

Send this to whoever owns your automations. DM REVIEW for a free check.

slides.title: Same reminder, two tools. *Which one fits?*
slides.sub: Make.com vs n8n for appointment reminders.

slides.title: Setup
slides.body: *Make.com:* hosted, visual, start in minutes. *n8n:* n8n Cloud or self-hosted; self-hosting needs a server and someone to update it.

slides.title: Cost model
slides.body: *Make.com* bills by usage credits (formerly operations) per month. *n8n* counts workflow executions on Cloud, or nothing per run when self-hosted. Check current plans before choosing.

slides.title: Patient data
slides.body: Self-hosted *n8n* keeps data on your own server. With either tool, send only what the reminder needs: *name, time, clinic.* No clinical notes.

slides.title: Our rule of thumb
slides.body: Small clinic, no IT person: *Make.com.* Several sites, many reminders or strict data rules: *n8n.*

slides.title: We'll recommend one, with reasons.
slides.sub: Tell us your booking system and reminder volume.

captions.ig:
Make.com or n8n for clinic appointment reminders?

02 Cost: Make bills by usage credits; n8n Cloud counts executions; self-hosted has no per-run fee (check current plans)
03 Data: send only name, time and clinic, never clinical notes
04 Our rule of thumb: small clinic, Make.com; several sites or strict data rules, n8n

slides.title: What goes into *a KYC check?*
slides.sub: How we built identity verification, step by step.

slides.title: Read the document
slides.body: OCR extracts name, date of birth and document number from the ID image, so nobody types them.

slides.title: Match the face
slides.body: Face matching compares a selfie with the photo on the ID and returns a similarity score.

slides.title: Screen the name
slides.body: AML screening checks the person against watchlists as part of the same flow.

slides.title: Keep a person on the edge cases
slides.body: Clear passes move on. Low scores and possible matches go to a *review dashboard* for a human decision.

slides.title: Expose it as an API
slides.body: Your product calls one REST API and gets a result it can act on, plus an audit trail.

slides.title: Plan KYC in from the start.

captions.ig:
What actually happens in a KYC check? Here is how we built Identixa, our identity verification platform:

01 OCR reads the ID document
02 Face matching compares a selfie with the ID photo
03 AML screening checks watchlists
04 Edge cases go to a human review dashboard
05 One REST API returns the result, with an audit trail

If your product needs identity checks, planning them in from the start saves rework later. Link in bio.

slides.title: The cheap option is not *always cheap at year three.*
Start with off-the-shelf when
slides.body: Your process is standard (invoicing, email, basic CRM) and a tool covers *80% of it* without workarounds.

slides.title: Watch the hidden costs
slides.body: Per-seat pricing as you grow, paid add-ons, and *staff time* spent on workarounds and exports.

slides.title: Go custom when
slides.body: The process is how you compete, nothing fits without heavy workarounds, or you need to own the data and the roadmap.

slides.title: Or do both
slides.body: Keep the SaaS tools that work and build the *missing piece* that connects them.
